markdown_report:
At 20% progress, prioritize a small, testable extension: **an edge-reliability-weighted directed-transition residual**, with multiple-source gating tested separately. Compare it with objective-only SASRec and the starting lexical residual. No new performance is established.

**Insights from the starting point.** (1) Distinct-item support can limit isolated-purchase effects. Repeated events from one item must not count as independent sources. (2) Recency weighting addresses stale evidence. Apply confidence after normalization so weak support remains weak. (3) Fixed lexical features provide inspectable specificity. Boilerplate and shared vocabulary nevertheless cannot establish usefulness or compatibility.

**Insights from related work.** (1) Collaboration and Transition [1] motivates directional associations. These encode behavioral progression without establishing complementarity. (2) Long/short-term modeling [2] motivates selecting persistent interests using recent context. A short window approximates this cheaply but can miss infrequent interests. (3) eSASRec [3] motivates an objective-only control. Electronics’ 16.04% negative-over-positive training-pair rate warrants investigation without diagnosing its cause. (4) SpotTarget [4] distinguishes training-target inclusion from held-out leakage. User-excluded graph diagnostics can expose self-contributed evidence, although frozen-weight ablations cannot remove parameter memorization. (5) Dunning [5] motivates caution about rare associations. Source frequency alone cannot establish individual-edge reliability.

**Framework and directions.** Separate evidence, temporal selection, reliability, and optimization:

| Idea | Evidence / temporal selection | O/F/U/M/D |
|---|---|---|
| A: Objective-only SASRec | Collaborative / existing attention | 2/6/3/8/2 |
| B: Starting lexical residual | Symmetric text / recent repeated support | 4/6/7/6/4 |
| C: Directed residual, selected family | Transitions / recent sources and distinct-user shrinkage | 3/6/7/7/5 |

Scores are prospective: originality, future potential, user alignment, model alignment, and implementation difficulty. A offers clean attribution but limited direct user-failure coverage. B offers specificity but risks boilerplate shortcuts. C offers directional evidence but risks rare-edge noise, popularity effects, and self-contributed training support. Its contribution is an incremental combination; efficient sparse scoring and diagnostic parity raise implementation difficulty.

**Selected algorithm.** Count training-only adjacent transitions and distinct contributing users per edge. Smooth destination probabilities toward training popularity, clip positive log-lift, and shrink each edge by distinct-user support. Aggregate across deduplicated recent sources with recency and source-reliability weights. Compare the bounded residual with and without the original two-source gate; do not presume gating improves sparse histories.

This targets broad associations lacking directional support and stale or isolated interactions outweighing repeated recent interests. Uniform 32-negative sampled softmax targets weak training-pair separation. Neither mechanism establishes compatibility, ownership, or unmet needs.

Compare A, B, ungated C, and gated C under the remaining shared budget. Preserve all four categories, seeds, routing, diagnostics, and predictor parity; select exclusively by pinned macro validation HR@10. Track coverage, support buckets, rank changes, and user-excluded graph sensitivity. Keep simulator judgments separate from sampled HR@10.

References: [1] [Collaboration and Transition](https://arxiv.org/abs/2311.01056); [2] [Long/short-term modeling](https://journal.hep.com.cn/fcs/EN/10.1007/s11704-025-41181-y); [3] [eSASRec](https://arxiv.org/abs/2508.06450); [4] [SpotTarget](https://arxiv.org/abs/2306.00899); [5] [Dunning](https://aclanthology.org/J93-1003/).

idea.description: Add an edge-reliability-weighted, bounded directed-transition residual to per-dataset SASRec. Aggregate training-derived directional evidence from distinct recent historical items, shrink edges using distinct-user support, and test the original requirement for two supporting sources as a separate ablation. Train with uniform multi-negative sampled softmax and compare against objective-only SASRec and the starting fixed lexical residual.
idea.motivation: The user diagnosis identifies broad historical association and stale or isolated interactions as two concrete failures. Directional evidence, recency weighting, and independently replicated edge support address these failures as predictive heuristics. Multiple-source gating may further reduce isolated-source effects, but sparse coverage makes its benefit uncertain. Electronics has a negative lower-tail training margin and 16.04% negative-over-positive pairs, motivating an objective comparison without establishing the cause of validation errors. The supplied prior score of 0.5863 is contextual evidence, not a demonstrated result for this proposal. Compatibility, duplication, dimensions, quantity, and unmet needs remain largely unresolved because the available histories and text provide insufficient supervision for reliable labels.
idea.implementation_notes:
Protocol and scope: retain Movies_and_TV, Industrial_and_Scientific, Electronics, and CDs_and_Vinyl as separate models with unchanged routing and splits. Keep DATA_DIR = os.environ['GAGC_DATA_DIR'], preprocessing seed 0, training seed 42, and the effective SASREC_EPOCHS default 200. All artifacts remain beneath the trial directory. Use one GPU. Do not access test labels, extra datasets, pretrained weights, unavailable metadata, or simulator traits. Only permitted histories, timestamps, titles, and descriptions may be used. The generic metadata examples do not authorize ratings, reviews, categories, prices, or stores. No shell actions, training, or measurements are claimed in this report.

Transition fitting: construct category-specific adjacent-transition counts C[a,b] exclusively from user_train histories in their existing chronological order. Count every adjacent nonpadding pair, including self-transitions; do not create edges across users. Let U[a,b] count distinct training users contributing that edge, counting each user once regardless of repeated occurrences. Let n[a] = sum_b C[a,b], d[b] = sum_a C[a,b], and T = sum_b d[b]. Over the N nonpadding items in the baseline training-visible catalog, define p0[b] = (d[b]+1)/(T+N). For tau=10, compute P(b|a) = (C[a,b]+tau*p0[b])/(n[a]+tau), L[a,b] = clip(log(P(b|a)/p0[b]), 0, 2), and E[a,b] = U[a,b]/(U[a,b]+2) * L[a,b]. Fix tau, clipping, and the distinct-user shrinkage constant before evaluation; do not tune them in the first family. For an unobserved edge, positive lift is zero, including a zero-outdegree source. Source reliability n[a]/(n[a]+tau) and edge reliability U[a,b]/(U[a,b]+2) address different uncertainties. Distinct users provide replication, not independent causal evidence. Save raw counts, user-support counts, priors, and resolved constants; retain raw edges even when their current positive lift is zero, because user-excluded diagnostics can change normalization.

Sparse implementation: never materialize an N-by-N matrix. Store raw edges in sorted CSR rows and optionally derive sorted int64 keys a*(N+1)+b for batched torch.searchsorted queries. Check insertion bounds before indexing, then verify exact key equality; absent keys return zero. Confirm the maximum key fits int64. CSR requires O(N+E_raw) storage, and sorted keys O(E_raw), excluding explicitly recorded per-user contributions. Chunk B-by-L-by-history-window-by-candidate queries to bound temporary memory. Full-catalog inference enumerates edges from at most 20 source rows, scatters evidence into candidate accumulators, and adds the residual to the existing collaborative score vector. Do not allocate all training-position-by-catalog scores. Measure sparse lookup and diagnostic cost within the search budget.

Prefix construction: at each supervised position use only that position's observed prefix. Take its last 20 valid events, deduplicate by retaining each item's latest occurrence, and keep each retained event's original age, with age zero for the latest event. Define w[a] = exp(-age[a]/5)*n[a]/(n[a]+tau), D = sum_a w[a], z[b] = sum_a w[a]*E[a,b]/max(D,1e-8), c[b] = sum_a w[a]*1[E[a,b]>0]/max(D,1e-8), and k[b] = sum_a 1[E[a,b]>0]. Unsupported sources remain in D. The ungated residual is R0[b] = c[b]*tanh(z[b]); the gated residual is R2[b] = 1[k[b]>=2]*R0[b]. Confidence c remains outside the normalized evidence score. Its additional attenuation is intentional and must be assessed through actual residual magnitude. Empty histories, absent edges, and zero-weight histories return exactly zero; one-source histories return zero only in the gated condition. Repetitions of a single historical ID never satisfy the two-source gate. Item event age is not elapsed wall-clock time; timestamps are not otherwise used in this first experiment.

Scoring: s[b] = h dot item_emb[b] + alpha*R[b], where alpha = 2*sigmoid(a), initialized by a = log(0.05/0.95), giving alpha=0.1. Since R lies in [0,1], each residual lies in [0,2] and changes any pairwise margin by at most 2 logit units. This scale is an engineering choice and can be weak relative to large collaborative logits. Report residual-to-collaborative-margin scale, amplitude trajectories, and actual rank changes. The ungated and gated conditions use identical scoring, normalization, initialization, and candidate rules except for the k>=2 mask. Do not add a separate popularity score, text branch, adaptive mining, or auxiliary loss to either transition condition.

Training objective: use 32 distinct uniform negatives per valid target, excluding padding, the target, and items observed in that position's prefix only. Do not consult future interactions or held-out labels for exclusions. If fewer than 32 eligible IDs exist, use all and mask unused slots. If none exist, omit that position from the loss. Draw negatives with a dedicated training generator seeded 42 so candidate sampling does not alter dropout or initialization RNG streams; share this procedure across all new conditions. Optimize masked cross-entropy over the positive at index zero and sampled negatives, averaging over eligible positions. Preserve the baseline backbone, optimizer, learning rate, batch size, regularization, validation schedule, and checkpoint rule. Record their actual resolved values from the host template before execution rather than inventing absent settings. This is a sampled ranking surrogate, not an unbiased full-softmax estimator; uniform sampling and observed-positive exclusion do not eliminate unknown false negatives.

Lexical comparator B: retain the starting fixed TF-IDF repeated-support design, rather than substituting an all-history ungated text pool. Per category, tokenize permitted title followed by description using lowercase Unicode alphanumeric tokens. Fit vocabulary and document frequencies on the baseline training-visible catalog, retaining at most 30,000 tokens in descending document-frequency order with lexical tie-breaking. Exclude tokens present in more than 20% of catalog documents, then retain the first 32 remaining tokens per item. Use binary term frequency, IDF(w)=log((1+N)/(1+df(w)))+1, and L2-normalized sparse item vectors; missing or entirely filtered text yields zero. Save vocabulary, IDF, token filtering, item rows, and catalog scope. For each prefix's last 20 events, set r_j=exp(-age_j/5) and u_j to the maximum TF-IDF cosine with another event having a distinct item ID; default to zero. Compute q=normalize(sum_j r_j*u_j*v_j), c_text=sum_j r_j*u_j/max(sum_j r_j,1e-8), and R_text[b]=c_text*dot(q,v_b), with zero output when q is zero. Padding and missing text cannot supply support; equal IDs cannot support each other. Use the same bounded amplitude parameterization and sampled-softmax objective as C, with no learned token encoder or auxiliary loss. Sparse query vectors may densify; chunk candidate products and avoid an item-by-item similarity matrix. This comparator tests evidence type as a bundle; differences from C cannot be attributed solely to direction because pooling and reliability also differ.

Controlled family: predeclare four complete four-category conditions: A, objective-only SASRec; B, fixed lexical residual; C0, edge-shrunk ungated transition residual; C2, the same transition residual with two-source gating. A versus C0 estimates incremental transition-branch value under the shared objective, C0 versus C2 isolates the hard gate, and B versus C tests alternative evidence bundles. Preserve an available pinned baseline separately, verifying its protocol before comparison. A versus an otherwise identical single-negative-BCE baseline is necessary to attribute changes to the objective; if no matched baseline exists, do not make that attribution. Do not add a fresh baseline training run without charging it to the same budget. Conditional probability, unshrunk lift, edge-count shrinkage, minimum-support filtering, adaptive gating, transition-only training, and scratch-trained text generalization remain future directions rather than an uncontrolled search grid. A transition-only scoring diagnostic can describe branch behavior, but it is not an equal-training-budget model comparison.

Budget and scheduling: first subtract every earlier training, diagnostic, debugging, and failed-trial GPU-second from 43,200. If none has been consumed, reserve 7,200 GPU-seconds for diagnostics and parity checks and allocate at most 9,000 to each of the four main conditions, or 2,250 per category. Otherwise allocate at most one-sixth of the remaining budget to the diagnostic reserve and divide the remainder equally among conditions and categories. Existing charged work is not reset by this report. Run at most 200 epochs and respect the unchanged checkpoint schedule. Record actual exposure and GPU time; retain complete-epoch checkpoints and the baseline checkpoint rule without silently changing evaluation timing. If a cap prevents a valid four-category result, mark that condition incomplete and do not rank a partial macro score. This family compares budget-limited methods; unequal completed epochs remain a limitation. Do not compensate failed conditions with unreported extra tuning.

Selection and uncertainty: use only the unchanged host protocol: 200 validation users/category, 99 unique negative candidates, evaluation seed 42, and equal-weight macro HR@10. Keep the incumbent on exact ties and preserve every trial result. Report all four category values, macro HR@10, exposure, and cost. One additional hit changes a category rate by 0.005 and the macro rate by 0.00125. If the host already exposes authorized per-user hit indicators, a paired category-stratified bootstrap can describe fixed-model uncertainty; otherwise state that such uncertainty is unavailable. Do not modify the evaluator, generate replacement validation candidates, claim seed robustness, or infer full-catalog quality from sampled HR@10. Multiple condition selection remains exploratory.

Training-target inclusion and shortcut diagnosis: full training-graph fitting is legitimate and differs from incorporating validation or test interactions, which is prohibited. However, a training target often contributes its own source-target edge, so both training margins and support coverage can be optimistic. On deterministic sampled training users, compare full-graph scores with scores from a graph excluding all contributions by that user. Subtract that user's adjacent counts from C and one from U for every edge the user contributed, then recompute affected source totals, destination totals, T, p0, smoothing, clipping, edge shrinkage, and source reliability. Keep catalog N fixed. Merely zeroing the current edge, retaining the original priors, or subtracting one occurrence is insufficient. Avoid pruning before this diagnostic; edges previously clipped to zero may become positive after normalization changes. Cache per-user sparse contributions and process users in bounded chunks. Use frozen trained weights and identical prefixes/candidates for paired comparisons. These ablations measure dependence on self-contributed graph structure and do not remove memorization in model weights or constitute validation leakage tests. Full cross-fitted retraining is stronger but outside the first family.

For user-excluded diagnostics, report paired changes in target score, positive-minus-negative margin, residual support, and rank within a fixed explicitly labeled diagnostic candidate set. Reuse supplied training-batch negatives where possible. If diagnostic ranks require extra candidates, generate unique training-only candidates with a separate analysis generator seeded 42, excluding prefix IDs and target, and document their count; never label the result as host validation HR@10. Separate raw-count buckets C=0, C=1, C=2–4, C>=5 and distinct-user buckets U=0, U=1, U=2–4, U>=5. Also report destination-frequency deciles, zero-support rate, one-source versus multiple-source coverage, and repeated-event prevalence. These expose rare-edge, popularity, and own-history shortcuts; they do not prove causal explanations. Validation support-bucket breakdowns are permissible only when authorized evaluator outputs already provide the required IDs and outcomes, without changing the evaluator.

Diagnostic adapter: preserve DiagnosisProbe(view, device).run_full_diagnosis(train_loader), returning metrics and metric_definitions, and the loader contract (None, sequence, positive, negative), each tensor B x L. Keep view.model as the actual trained nn.Module and view.item_emb as its collaborative embedding. Have log2feats return a packed tensor containing collaborative features and the prefix context required by the selected scorer at each causal position. For C, pack the at-most-20 source IDs and original event ages; store IDs in a representation that round-trips exactly, such as float64 packing with explicit integer recovery and range checks, while casting h back to its model dtype for scoring. For B, pack the at-most-20 original event IDs and ages needed to reconstruct its fixed lexical support. Keep item embeddings and trainable states inside the actual module, and store graph/text artifacts as persisted nontrainable state loaded identically for training and inference. predict_score must handle position-aligned items and candidate lists using an explicit documented broadcasting contract, unpack context, and reproduce the actual fused score. Preserve user_train, meta_data, and review_data without inventing unavailable fields. Keep causal-prefix, finite-value, and training-margin probes; use fused scores. Add defined support coverage, residual magnitude, amplitude, and user-exclusion sensitivity metrics. Label embedding cosine alignment as descriptive, not proof of collapse. Return item-category breakdowns as unavailable with the stated reason.

Simulator use: twenty real training users, five per category, receive full-catalog unseen-item recommendations under the native protocol. Exclude historical IDs. Assess broad association, stale or isolated evidence, duplication, unsupported use cases, and unassessable practical fit separately. Available titles and descriptions may support some distinctions, but do not manufacture compatibility, ownership, quantity requirements, satisfied needs, or latent traits. Simulator feedback remains diagnostic and cannot replace macro HR@10 selection.

Inference parity: update the predictor writer to emit the matching architecture and load category-specific weights, counts or derived sparse evidence, priors, vocabulary where applicable, configuration, and learned amplitude from artifacts beneath the trial directory. Preserve working/predict.py routing, truncation, padding, deduplication, event ages, and candidate order. Use the full permitted training graph for validation and final inference; never add held-out edges. Full-graph training and inference use the same graph, while user-excluded graphs are diagnostic ablations only. Verify generated-predictor score parity on deterministic training-visible fixtures for empty histories, repeated IDs, one source, two sources, absent edges, missing text, zero-outdegree items, searchsorted boundary keys, and mixed-category routing. Run probes on the actual trained architecture. No implementation, execution, successful parity check, or validation gain is claimed here.
idea.pseudocode:
CONFIG: categories=FOUR_CATEGORIES, preprocessing_seed=0, training_seed=42
CONFIG: epochs=env_default_200, history_window=20, recency_scale=5
CONFIG: tau=10, distinct_user_shrinkage=2, lift_clip=2, negatives=32

fit_graph(training_histories, N):
    C = counts_of_adjacent_pairs_within_each_training_user()
    U = distinct_training_user_count_for_each_edge()
    n = outgoing_counts(C)
    d = destination_counts(C)
    p0 = (d + 1) / (sum(d) + N)
    for observed edge (a,b):
        P = (C[a,b] + tau*p0[b]) / (n[a] + tau)
        lift = clip(log(P / p0[b]), 0, 2)
        E[a,b] = U[a,b] / (U[a,b] + 2) * lift
    save_raw_counts_support_priors_and_sorted_sparse_edges()
    return E, n

transition_residual(prefix, candidates, gate):
    events = last_20_valid_events(prefix)
    sources, ages = keep_latest_occurrence_per_ID_preserving_original_event_age(events)
    w = exp(-ages/5) * n[sources]/(n[sources]+tau)
    evidence = exact_sparse_lookup(E, sources, candidates, missing=0)
    supported = evidence > 0
    denominator = max(sum(w), 1e-8)
    z = sum_sources(w * evidence) / denominator
    confidence = sum_sources(w * supported) / denominator
    R = confidence * tanh(z)
    if gate:
        R *= (sum_sources(supported) >= 2)
    return R

score(prefix_features, candidates, condition):
    h, context = unpack(prefix_features)
    base = dot(h, item_emb(candidates))
    if condition == A:
        return base
    if condition == B:
        R = fixed_TFIDF_repeated_support_residual(context, candidates)
    else:
        R = transition_residual(context, candidates, gate=(condition == C2))
    return base + 2*sigmoid(a)*R

remaining = 43200 - all_previous_charged_GPU_seconds
reserve = min(7200, remaining/6)
condition_cap = (remaining-reserve)/4
for condition in [A, B, C0, C2]:
    for category in FOUR_CATEGORIES:
        reset_training_seed(42)
        initialize_same_backbone_and_dedicated_negative_generator(seed=42)
        initialize_a(log(0.05/0.95)) if residual_enabled
        for batch in unchanged_loader(category):
            features = causal_log2feats_with_required_prefix_context(batch.sequence)
            candidates, mask = positive_plus_32_unique_uniform_negatives(
                exclude=padding_target_and_observed_prefix_only)
            loss = eligible_position_mean(masked_CE(score(features,candidates), target=0))
            optimize(loss)
            preserve_checkpoint_schedule_and_respect_category_time_cap(condition_cap/4)
        save_weights_config_sparse_artifacts_and_matching_predictor()
        verify_generated_predictor_parity_on_training_visible_fixtures()
        run_adapted_DiagnosisProbe_with_fused_scores()
    if all_four_categories_have_valid_results:
        record_unchanged_host_macro_validation_HR10()
    else:
        mark_condition_incomplete()

for sampled_training_user in deterministic_diagnostic_sample:
    excluded_C = global_C - all_adjacent_counts_from_user
    excluded_U = global_U - indicator_user_contributed_each_edge
    excluded_graph = recompute_all_affected_normalization_and_evidence(excluded_C, excluded_U)
    compare_frozen_model_scores_on_identical_prefixes_and_diagnostic_candidates(
        full_graph, excluded_graph)
    report_paired_margin_rank_support_changes_by_count_and_user_support_bucket()

select_complete_condition_by_pinned_macro_HR10_with_incumbent_tie_break()
# Keep simulator judgments and training-graph diagnostics separate from validation metrics.
# Held-out interactions never enter graph construction, exclusions, or calibration.

originality.positive: Combining candidate-specific recent support, distinct-user edge shrinkage, and a separately tested multiple-source gate gives an inspectable adaptation tied to the observed failures.
originality.negative: Directed transitions, popularity-normalized association, shrinkage, recency pooling, and additive fusion are established techniques. The contribution is incremental, and no verified novelty claim is warranted.

future_potential.positive: Separating directional evidence, edge replication, temporal selection, and gating supports clear experiments and later sparse-text generalization.
future_potential.negative: Sparse support, outdated associations, popularity confounding, and training-target self-evidence may limit gains. Predictive edges cannot resolve practical compatibility or unmet needs.

code_difficulty.positive: Retains SASRec and uses fixed sparse statistics with a small additive scoring branch, avoiding learned graph encoders and pretrained text models.
code_difficulty.negative: Efficient causal sparse queries, distinct-user bookkeeping, correctly normalized user-exclusion diagnostics, lexical comparison, and generated-predictor parity require substantial care.

related_work.title: Collaboration and Transition
contributions: The supplied search summary describes weighted directed transition graphs and transition distillation into sequential recommendation.
Motivates using behavioral direction rather than symmetric lexical similarity.
limitations: Does not establish effectiveness of the proposed edge shrinkage or multiple-source gate on the pinned benchmark.
Transition associations do not identify compatibility, complementarity, or unmet needs.

related_work.title: Hierarchical long/short-term modeling
contributions: The supplied summary describes multiple persistent preference vectors selected using recent features and time encoding.
Motivates conditioning historical evidence on recent behavior.
limitations: A fixed recent window is a simplified adaptation and does not reproduce the reported architecture.
Recent behavior can be noisy, while infrequent persistent interests can fall outside the window.

related_work.title: eSASRec
contributions: The supplied summary identifies sampled softmax and LiGR layers as components of a strong SASRec configuration.
Supports an objective-only control before attributing gains to additional evidence.
limitations: Does not prove uniform sampled softmax improves this benchmark.
Combined architectural and objective changes cannot isolate the proposed residual's contribution.

related_work.title: GCL4SR
contributions: The supplied reflection summary provides an example of global weighted item-transition graphs and degree normalization.
Supports sparse global behavioral evidence as an established modeling component.
limitations: Does not establish the proposed reliability formula, recent-source aggregation, or gating rule.
Global training graphs can contain the same edges used as training targets, making in-sample recovery optimistic.

related_work.title: SpotTarget
contributions: The supplied summary distinguishes training-target inclusion and associated overfitting from held-out-target leakage.
Motivates examining dependence on self-contributed graph evidence.
limitations: Evidence comes from adjacent link-prediction research rather than this sequential-recommendation benchmark.
User-excluded frozen-weight graph diagnostics are a proposed adaptation, not an established standard or a substitute for cross-fitted retraining.

related_work.title: Accurate Methods for the Statistics of Surprise and Coincidence
contributions: Supports caution when interpreting association estimates derived from small counts.
Motivates distinguishing source frequency from individual-edge reliability.
limitations: Does not validate the proposed distinct-user shrinkage constant or positive log-lift scorer.
Evidence about lexical association does not establish recommendation gains under uniform sampled candidates.

related_work.title: Don't Recommend the Obvious: Estimate Probability Ratios
contributions: The supplied summary connects probability-ratio scoring with popularity-sampled evaluation.
Highlights that association-score suitability depends on the candidate protocol.
limitations: Transfer to this benchmark's pinned negative-candidate protocol requires validation.
Positive log-lift should remain an empirical scoring choice rather than a claimed optimal objective.

related_work.title: PyTorch sparse CSR tensors and searchsorted
contributions: Documents sparse CSR storage for row-oriented edge enumeration.
Together with https://docs.pytorch.org/docs/stable/generated/torch.searchsorted.html, provides primitives for sparse lookup without dense item-by-item matrices.
limitations: Primitive availability does not establish end-to-end speed or GPU memory suitability.
Missing-key checks, query chunking, dtype handling, and inference parity remain implementation responsibilities.

related_work.title: scikit-learn TfidfVectorizer
contributions: Documents vocabulary fitting, document-frequency filtering, IDF weighting, and normalization primitives.
Supports reproducible fixed lexical representations without pretrained weights.
limitations: The supplied starting comparator requires custom token ordering, truncation, binary term frequency, and repeated-support pooling.
Library defaults or the newly suggested all-history unigram comparator would change the original comparison and must not be substituted silently.
